questiontext.text:
The two triangles below have some equal parts marked. Matching tick marks (|, ||, |||) show sides that are equal, and matching arcs show angles that are equal. A small square shows a right angle.

[[jsxgraph width='500px' height='500px']] var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-1.5, 5.0, 13.8, -2.0], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); var V1 = {#V1#}, V2 = {#V2#}; var ST1 = {#st1#}, ST2 = {#st2#}; var AA1 = {#aa1#}, AA2 = {#aa2#}; var Lab1 = ['A', 'B', 'C'], Lab2 = ['D', 'E', 'F']; function centroid(V) { return [(V[0][0] + V[1][0] + V[2][0]) / 3, (V[0][1] + V[1][1] + V[2][1]) / 3]; } function labelOffset(V, i) { var c = centroid(V); var dx = V[i][0] - c[0], dy = V[i][1] - c[1]; var m = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) || 1; return [16 * dx / m, 16 * dy / m]; } function drawTicks(p, q, n) { var mx = (p[0] + q[0]) / 2, my = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2; var dx = q[0] - p[0], dy = q[1] - p[1]; var len = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) || 1; var ux = dx / len, uy = dy / len; // along the side var nx = -uy, ny = ux; // perpendicular var h = 0.17, sp = 0.14, start = -(n - 1) / 2; for (var j = 0; j < n; j++) { var off = (start + j) * sp; var cx = mx + ux * off, cy = my + uy * off; b.create('segment', [[cx - nx * h, cy - ny * h], [cx + nx * h, cy + ny * h]], {strokeColor: '#d00000', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } } function drawAngle(pA, pV, pB, code) { if (code === 4) { // right-angle square var vx = pV.X(), vy = pV.Y(); var a = [pA.X() - vx, pA.Y() - vy], bb = [pB.X() - vx, pB.Y() - vy]; var la = Math.sqrt(a[0] * a[0] + a[1] * a[1]) || 1; var lb = Math.sqrt(bb[0] * bb[0] + bb[1] * bb[1]) || 1; var ua = [a[0] / la, a[1] / la], ub = [bb[0] / lb, bb[1] / lb]; var s = 0.42; var c1 = [vx + ua[0] * s, vy + ua[1] * s]; var c2 = [vx + ua[0] * s + ub[0] * s, vy + ua[1] * s + ub[1] * s]; var c3 = [vx + ub[0] * s, vy + ub[1] * s]; b.create('segment', [c1, c2], {strokeColor: '#0a7d00', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [c2, c3], {strokeColor: '#0a7d00', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } else { for (var j = 0; j < code; j++) { b.create('angle', [pA, pV, pB], { radius: 0.55 + j * 0.17, withLabel: false, fillColor: '#0a7d00', fillOpacity: 0, strokeColor: '#0a7d00', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false }); } } } function drawTriangle(V, Lab, ST, AA) { var P = []; for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { P.push(b.create('point', V[i], { name: Lab[i], fixed: true, size: 1, fillColor: '#222', strokeColor: '#222', label: {fontSize: 15, offset: labelOffset(V, i)} })); } b.create('segment', [P[0], P[1]], {strokeColor: '#0057b7', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [P[1], P[2]], {strokeColor: '#0057b7', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [P[2], P[0]], {strokeColor: '#0057b7', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); for (var k = 0; k < 3; k++) { // side k is opposite vertex k if (ST[k] > 0) { drawTicks(V[(k + 1) % 3], V[(k + 2) % 3], ST[k]); } } // signed area: >0 = counter-clockwise, <0 = clockwise (flipped copy) var ccw = ((V[1][0] - V[0][0]) * (V[2][1] - V[0][1]) - (V[1][1] - V[0][1]) * (V[2][0] - V[0][0])) > 0; for (var k = 0; k < 3; k++) { // angle at vertex k if (AA[k] > 0) { var arm1 = ccw ? P[(k + 1) % 3] : P[(k + 2) % 3]; var arm2 = ccw ? P[(k + 2) % 3] : P[(k + 1) % 3]; drawAngle(arm1, P[k], arm2, AA[k]); // order keeps the arc on the interior } } } drawTriangle(V1, Lab1, ST1, AA1); drawTriangle(V2, Lab2, ST2, AA2); [[/jsxgraph]]

Which congruence test proves that the two triangles are congruent? If the marked information is not enough to guarantee congruence, choose “not necessarily congruent”.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

{@casewhy@}

Answer: {@ansdisp@}.

Remember the valid tests for triangle congruence: SSS, SAS (the equal angle must be between the two equal sides), ASA and AAS, and RHS for right-angled triangles. Equal angles alone (AAA) give similar triangles, and two sides with a non-included angle (SSA) do not fix the triangle.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: Look again — the marked parts here are enough to prove the triangles congruent. Count the tick marks (equal sides) and arcs (equal angles), and check whether an equal angle sits between two equal sides.

Be careful: the marks here do not pin down a unique triangle. Equal angles fix the shape but not the size, and two sides with a non-included equal angle can be arranged into two different triangles. Check whether enough sides are marked equal to fix the size.

falsefeedback.text: The triangles are congruent, but that is not the matching test. Re-read the marks: are you given three equal sides, two sides and the angle between them, two angles and a side, or a right angle with the hypotenuse and a side?

qtest.description: Choosing "not congruent" on a congruent variant is wrong and routed to saidnone. (Valid on seeds whose answer is a real test.)
